proposals.evidence: Exact match to the Palula first-person singular oblique-stem continuation ma; the survey gloss is the first-person pronoun.
proposals.sourceEvidence: ma base of singular oblique cases of 1st person pronoun: acc. mā́m, inst. máyā, dat. máhyam, gen. máma, encl. mē. Pa. maṁ, mayā, mayhaṁ, mama; Aś. acc. maṁ, inst. mayā, gen. shah. man. maa, gir. kāl. dh. mama; NiDoc. gen. dat. mama, mahi; Pk. acc. maṁ, mamaṁ, inst. maē, gen. mama, majjhaṁ, Ap. inst. maï˜. — Except in some peripheral NIA. languages a form based for the most part on Pk. inst. maē (with substitution of nominal inst. ending -eṁ < -ēna) has taken the place of old nominative ahám; Gy. eur. me 'I', pal. ắma; Chil. Gau. Sv. Phal. Sh. ma (but Phal. inst. mē, mī), S.srk. mā̃, mū̃; L. maĩ, mε῀ nom. and inst., P. maĩ, WPah.jaun. mē̃ (nom. also hāũ, aũ); Garh. maĩ, mĩ (inst. maĩn), Ku. maĩ, mī (inst. maĩle), N. ma, emph. maĩ (inst. maile), A. maï, B. (vulgar) mui, Or. mu, mũ; OAw. maïṁ nom. and inst.; H. maĩ (inst. maĩne), OMarw. mẽ, M. mī˜, mī. — Other forms: Pr. əm gen.; Tir. masi 'to me'; Kho. ma acc. and gen.; Tor. Sv. mī gen.; K. mĕ dat. inst. abl.; S. encl. -mi 'of, to, by me' < mē, L. encl. -m; WPah.bhad. maĩ inst. (aũ nom.), G. mε῀; Si. mama nom.; — H. mujh obl.; OG. majha dat., M. maj̈ obl., māj̈hā 'my', Ko. majjo. — The genitive is replaced by a declinable adjective with various suffixes: Gaw. mōna, Tir. myāna, K. myônᵘ; — Gy. gr. minro, SEeur. moi̦ó m., mei̦í f., L. maĩḍā, maiḍā; — Ap. mahāriya-, mēra-, WP. mε῀rā, P. merā, WPah. jaun. Garh. Ku. N. mero, A. mohora, mora, Or. mohara, OAw. moraü, H. merā, OMarw. meraü, OG. māharaü, G. mārũ. — See ahám, māmaká-. MAṀH 'give': máhas-². Addenda: ma-: Kho. ma 'me' obl. BKhoT 70; WPah.kṭg. mũ 'I'; Md. ma 'I, me' (gen. ma-ge, dat. mařař). †mámat. †makkaṇa- see matkuṇa-².

(child's language) larm, lear, leye after leg, lip); Gmb. dōš 'hand', Shum. aste-m, Gaw. hast (hāth 'forearm' ← Ind.), Kal.urt. hast, rumb. has (st. hast-); Kho. host 'hand, arm, cubit'; Tor. hΛtth m. 'hand', Kand. hath, Mai. hā, ky. hā̃ (obl. hātha); Sv. hatha 'hand, arm', Phal. hāt f. (ā hāth 'one cubit i.e. from elbow to finger tip'); Sh.gil. hăt m. 'hand, cubit', koh. gur. jij. hăth m., pales. hatth; K. atha, dat. athas m. 'hand, forearm', rām. ḍoḍ. hatth, pog. āht; S. hathu m. 'hand', L. P. hatth m., WPah.bhad. bhal. paṅ. hatth, cur. hatt, pāḍ. hat, (Joshi) hāth m.; Ku. hāth 'hand, arm, cubit'; N. hāt 'hand, forarm'; A. hāt 'hand, cubit'; B. hāt 'arm', Or. hāta; Bi. Mth. proposals.evidence: Turner’s manuṣya family includes Palula mīś husband/person; this is a semantic expansion within the same human noun, with puruṣa interference discussed in the wider family.
proposals.sourceEvidence: manuṣyà 'human', m. 'human being, man' RV. [Collides in various degrees with púruṣa- and also has various degrees of shortening, due prob. to use as a term of relationahip and address. — mánuṣa-] Pa. manussa- m. 'man', Aś.shah. man. manuśa-, gir. manusa-, kāl. manuṣa-, NiDoc. maṁnuśa, Pk. maṇussa-, maṇūsa- m., Gy. arm. manus (or < mā́nuṣa-), pal. mánŭs, pers. môness, Woṭ. maniš m.; L. maṇus 'man', múṇas m. 'husband', mult. muṇs, muṛs, awāṇ. muṇus, P. munas, muns, munsṛā m., WPah. bhad. muṇaś, cur. muṇś; Bi. Mth. manus 'man, person'. — X púruṣa-: Gy. eur. murš 'man, brave young man, boy'; S. mursu m. 'man, husband', L.khet. murs; — Pr. muš, mūšū (or < mártya- ?); Sh.gil. mušā́ 'man', koh. pales. jij. mušā 'husband', Ku. muso. — X MIA. purisa- s.v. púruṣa-: Aś.dh. jau. and all E inscrr. munisa-, WPah.bhal. miniś 'man', mεṇś 'husband'; A. munih 'man, hired farmworker'; B. munis 'day labourer', minsā 'fellow (contemptuous)'; Or. maṇisa 'man, servant, labourer', pilā m° 'a mere child', (Sambhalpur) munus, (Medinīpur) munisa 'labourer'; Ko. munis 'man'; Si. minisā, minihā 'man', miniya, minī 'corpse'; Md. mīhu 'man'; — Bshk. mīš, mī˜š 'young man, husband' (pl. mānuš); Sv. miš 'husband', Phal. mēš, mīš (pl. mōša, māšə), Ku. mais; — with unexpl. -s-: Shum. maĩsa, °se 'man', Niṅg. maisə. — X mā́nuṣa- or poss. mártya-: Dm. mâš 'men' (pl. of mač < mártya-); Kho. moš 'man, husband', Mai. "māsh", WPah.bhal. mā̃ś (after which ṭhḷā̃ś 'woman' ~ strī́- in ṭhḷā̃ś-miniś 'woman and man'). — Corresponding feminine forms (cf. mānuṣī- f. MBh., manuṣī- f. lex.): Wg. mō˜̈šī 'wife, woman' (NTS xvii 279 poss. < *mā̃syakī-), Paš.lauṛ. māšī, chil. mō̃šī, Shum. mä̃išī, Gaw. mašī́. amanuṣya-, manuṣyatvá-; manuṣyamātra-, *manuṣyarūpa-, manuṣyalōká-. Addenda: manuṣyà-: Garh. maṇsa 'man' (pl.?); Md. mini-kiru 'breast milk', mini-marā 'executing'; mīs, mīhā (pl. mīhun) 'man, people'; Kho. moš 'man'? BKhoT 71.
